title: Advanced TCR Repertoire Analysis
text: neighborhood test asks key biological question: antigen specificity encoded TCR sequence similarity? TCR, defines “neighborhood” (TCRs within distance radius), tests whether variable interest (e.g., epitope label) enriched neighborhood compared overall dataset. significant result (low adjusted p-value, high odds ratio) means knowing TCR’s sequence tells something specificity — nearby TCRs tend recognize antigen. p-values adjusted multiple testing using Benjamini-Hochberg procedure (controls false discovery rate). multi-level categorical variables, use chi-squared test:
code: # Use a mixed-epitope subset for a meaningful test mixed <- dash[dash$epitope %in% c("PA", "NP"), ] mixed$is_PA <- ifelse(mixed$epitope == "PA", "PA", "other")  result <- neighborhood_test(   mixed, organism = "mouse",   variable = mixed$is_PA,   radius = 50, test = "fisher" )  head(result[order(result$p_adjusted), c("index", "n_neighbors", "odds_ratio",                                          "p_value", "p_adjusted")]) #>     index n_neighbors odds_ratio     p_value   p_adjusted #> 52     52          42        Inf 1.31689e-14 2.123907e-13 #> 72     72          42        Inf 1.31689e-14 2.123907e-13 #> 170   170          42        Inf 1.31689e-14 2.123907e-13 #> 171   171          42        Inf 1.31689e-14 2.123907e-13 #> 174   174          42        Inf 1.31689e-14 2.123907e-13 #> 175   175          42        Inf 1.31689e-14 2.123907e-13 result_chi <- neighborhood_test(   dash, organism = "mouse",   variable = dash$epitope,   radius = 50, test = "chisq" )

title: Comparing TCR Repertoires
text: Biological question: two samples share clonotypes? tcr_repertoire_overlap() compares clone sharing two samples using three complementary metrics: Jaccard index: fraction unique clonotypes shared? (presence/absence ) Morisita-Horn: two samples share dominant clonotypes? (abundance-weighted) Overlap coefficient: fraction smaller sample’s clonotypes found larger sample? Jaccard 0 means shared CDR3-beta sequences PA NP responses — epitopes drive completely distinct TCR populations. expected well-separated viral epitopes.
code: # Create named count vectors (names = clonotype identifiers) pa_counts <- table(pa$cdr3b) np_counts <- table(np$cdr3b)  ov <- tcr_repertoire_overlap(pa_counts, np_counts) ov #> $jaccard #> [1] 0.002645503 #>  #> $morisita_horn #> [1] 0.0004578907 #>  #> $overlap_coef #> [1] 0.006711409

title: Comparing TCR Repertoires
text: Biological question: immune responses dominated expanded clones, broadly polyclonal? highly clonal response (clonality near 1) suggests strong antigen-driven expansion specific T cell clones. diverse response (clonality near 0) suggests either polyclonal response insufficient stimulation. Interpreting results: n_clones (richness): many distinct clonotypes detected. clonality: 0 = maximally diverse, 1 = single dominant clone. Epitopes high clonality strong clonal expansions. effective_n: “many equally-abundant clonotypes give diversity?” Lower effective_n relative n_clones means repertoire dominated clones. gini: Inequality clone sizes. High Gini means clones dominate; low Gini means clones evenly distributed.
code: diversity_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(epitopes, function(ep) {     counts <- dash$count[dash$epitope == ep]     div <- tcr_diversity(counts, order = 2, ci = FALSE)     data.frame(         epitope = ep,         n_clones = tcr_richness(counts),         clonality = round(tcr_clonality(counts), 3),         shannon = round(tcr_shannon_entropy(counts), 3),         simpson = round(div$entropy, 3),         effective_n = round(div$effective_number, 1),         gini = round(tcr_gini(counts), 3),         stringsAsFactors = FALSE     ) }))  diversity_table #>   epitope n_clones clonality shannon simpson effective_n  gini #> 1      F2      117     0.032   4.610   0.994       161.0 0.236 #> 2    m139       87     0.039   4.291   0.991       105.9 0.255 #> 3     M38      158     0.094   4.586   0.983        60.4 0.469 #> 4     M45      291     0.013   5.600   0.999       812.9 0.140 #> 5      NP      305     0.083   5.243   0.991       115.6 0.462 #> 6      PA      324     0.052   5.482   0.996       238.4 0.378 #> 7     PB1      642     0.031   6.267   0.998       654.4 0.265

title: Getting Started with tcrdistR
text: TCRdist? TCRdist quantifies similar two TCR sequences . aligns CDR3 regions TCRs, scores amino acid match/mismatch using biochemical similarity matrix (BSD4, derived BLOSUM62), adds penalty insertions/deletions (gaps), adds distance germline-encoded CDR1, CDR2, CDR2.5 loops (looked V-gene). Lower distance means similar TCRs. TCRs small distances (roughly < 50) often recognize antigen. core function tcrdist_matrix() computes dense N x N pairwise distance matrix. use subset 50 PA-specific TCRs speed: entry integer TCRdist value. Identical TCRs distance 0; typical distances range 0 ~400. rough guide: 0–25: similar; likely recognize epitope similar binding mode. 25–75: Moderately similar; may share specificity. 75–200: Distantly related; different CDR3 V-gene usage. > 200: Unrelated.

title: Getting Started with tcrdistR
text: distance functions accept components parameter compute distances specific TCR regions. lets ask focused biological questions: CDR3 ("cdr3"): captures unique rearrangement-derived binding interface — variable part TCR. V-region ("v_region"): captures germline-encoded contacts (CDR1, CDR2, CDR2.5) interact MHC molecule. Single chain ("alpha" "beta"): useful suspect one chain dominates antigen recognition. Available presets: "" (default), "cdr3", "v_region", "alpha", "beta". Individual terms: "va", "cdr3a", "vb", "cdr3b".
code: # CDR3 only (both chains, no V-region) d_cdr3 <- tcrdist_matrix(pa_sub, "mouse", components = "cdr3")  # V-region only (CDR1 + CDR2 + CDR2.5) d_v <- tcrdist_matrix(pa_sub, "mouse", components = "v_region")  # Components are additive: v_region + cdr3 = all d_all <- tcrdist_matrix(pa_sub, "mouse") stopifnot(all(abs((d_v + d_cdr3) - d_all) < 1e-10))  # Single chain d_alpha <- tcrdist_matrix(pa_sub, "mouse", components = "alpha") d_beta  <- tcrdist_matrix(pa_sub, "mouse", components = "beta") stopifnot(all(abs((d_alpha + d_beta) - d_all) < 1e-10))  # Custom combination d_custom <- tcrdist_matrix(pa_sub, "mouse", components = c("cdr3a", "vb"))

title: Glossary of Terms
text: AIRR Adaptive Immune Receptor Repertoire. community standard format storing immune receptor sequencing data tab-separated files. CDR1, CDR2 Complementarity-Determining Regions 1 2. Encoded entirely germline V-gene segment. primarily contact MHC molecule rather peptide antigen. CDR2.5 (HV4) tcrdist-specific term fourth hypervariable loop CDR2 CDR3. region makes additional MHC contacts included TCRdist V-region distance. CDR3 Complementarity-Determining Region 3. variable part TCR, formed V(D)J recombination. primary determinant antigen specificity — amino acid sequence loop directly contacts peptide antigen. Clone / Clonotype unique TCR sequence defined V-gene CDR3 combination. “clone” refers T cell population sharing sequence; “clonotype” sequence identity . Meta-clonotype group similar TCRs (within distance threshold) found across multiple individuals. represent convergent immune responses different people independently generate similar TCRs antigen. Meta-clonotypes can serve biomarkers antigen exposure. Public clonotype TCR sequence shared across multiple unrelated individuals, suggesting convergent selection driven common antigen. Repertoire full collection TCR sequences biological sample. V-region portion TCR encoded V gene segment, encompassing CDR1, CDR2, CDR2.5 loops. germline-encoded regions less variable CDR3 primarily contact MHC molecule.

title: Glossary of Terms
text: BLOSUM62 BLOcks SUbstitution Matrix, version 62. widely used scoring matrix protein evolution research quantifies often one amino acid substitutes another related proteins. Biochemically similar amino acids get high scores. BSD4 matrix BLOSUM62-derived substitution matrix rescaled specifically TCR distance calculations (Dash et al., 2017). default scoring matrix used TCRdist. Gap penalty aligning two CDR3 sequences different lengths, gap (insertion deletion) must introduced one positions. gap penalty (default: 12) distance cost added gap position, reflecting insertions/deletions rarer amino acid substitutions. Hamming distance simplest sequence comparison: count number positions two equal-length sequences different characters. Pairwise distance distance computed every possible pair set. N TCRs, produces N x N symmetric matrix entry (, j) distance TCR TCR j. Substitution matrix table scoring similarity pairs amino acids. High scores indicate biochemically similar amino acids frequently interchange evolution (e.g., leucine isoleucine). TCRdist specific distance metric used package. sums: (1) CDR3 alignment distance (using BSD4 matrix optimal gap placement), weighted 3x, plus (2) V-region distance CDR1, CDR2, CDR2.5 loops. Lower distance = similar TCRs. Distances ~50 often indicate TCRs recognize antigen.

title: Glossary of Terms
text: Clonality measure dominated repertoire clonotypes. Calculated 1 - (Shannon entropy / log(number clonotypes)). Ranges 0 (clonotypes equally abundant) 1 (single dominant clone). Effective number species number equally-abundant clonotypes give diversity index value. Converts abstract diversity score intuitive count. example, effective number 50 means repertoire behaves 50 equally-abundant clonotypes. Gini index measure inequality clonotype abundances, borrowed economics. 0 = clonotypes equally abundant (perfect equality); 1 = one clonotype cells (maximum inequality). Hill numbers family diversity indices parameterized order q. q=0 gives species richness (number clonotypes), q=1 gives Shannon diversity, q=2 gives Simpson’s diversity. Higher orders give weight abundant clonotypes. Jaccard index fraction clonotypes shared two samples: |intersection| / |union|. Ignores abundance; considers presence/absence. Ranges 0 (shared clonotypes) 1 (identical sets). Morisita-Horn index abundance-weighted overlap measure two samples. Unlike Jaccard, accounts many copies clonotype present. Two samples sharing single dominant clonotype high Morisita-Horn value even differ rare clonotypes. Odds ratio neighborhood tests, ratio odds target category inside versus outside TCR’s neighborhood. Values > 1 indicate enrichment; values < 1 indicate depletion. p-value (adjusted) probability observing result extreme chance, corrected fact many tests performed simultaneously (one per TCR). tcrdistR uses Benjamini-Hochberg correction, controls false discovery rate. threshold 0.05 means 5% significant results expected false positives. Shannon entropy information-theoretic measure diversity: H = -sum(p * log(p)) p proportion clonotype. Higher entropy = diverse. S equally-abundant clonotypes, H = log(S). Simpson’s diversity probability two randomly chosen TCRs sample different clonotypes. Higher values = diverse. Ranges 0 1. Species richness count distinct clonotypes sample. simplest diversity measure — ignores abundances entirely.

title: Glossary of Terms
text: Dense matrix standard matrix stores every value. N x N distance matrix uses approximately 8 * N^2 bytes memory (e.g., ~800 MB 10,000 TCRs). Eigenvalues PCA, eigenvalues quantify much variance principal component captures. Larger eigenvalues indicate important components. Examining dropoff eigenvalues helps decide many components meaningful. Kernel PCA variant PCA works similarity (kernel) matrix rather raw data coordinates. Used embed TCRdist distances low-dimensional space visualization. “Linear kernel” applies simple distance--similarity conversion; “Gaussian kernel” uses exponential transformation emphasizes local structure. PCA (Principal Component Analysis) method reduce high-dimensional data key axes (components) capture variation. Points close together PCA space similar TCR sequences. first components typically explain biologically meaningful differences. Sparse matrix matrix stores non-zero (-threshold) entries. distance matrices, entries threshold stored, dramatically reducing memory usage. Stored dgCMatrix object Matrix package. UMAP (Uniform Manifold Approximation Projection) nonlinear dimensionality reduction method often separates clusters better PCA. Points close together UMAP space share similar TCR sequences. Unlike PCA, UMAP preserves local neighborhood structure preserve global distances.

text: Visualize pairwise distance matrix heatmap. Note plot_tcrdist_heatmap() takes precomputed distance matrix, TCR data.frame:  hierarchical clustering reordering (default) custom labels:
code: library(ggplot2)  dist_mat <- tcrdist_matrix(pa_sub, organism = "mouse") plot_tcrdist_heatmap(dist_mat) # Use a small subset with unique labels for readability small_mat <- dist_mat[1:20, 1:20] plot_tcrdist_heatmap(   small_mat,   labels = paste0(pa_sub$cdr3b[1:20], " (", seq_len(20), ")"),   cluster = TRUE,   title = "PA-specific TCR Distances" )

text: C++-accelerated TCR distance calculations T-cell receptor repertoire analysis. Computes pairwise TCRdist distances incorporating V-region CDR3 sequence comparisons using BLOSUM62-derived substitution matrices. Supports paired alpha-beta single-chain (beta-alpha-) input, per-component distance decomposition, targets feature parity Python tcrdist3.

title: TCR Distance Calculations for T-Cell Receptor Repertoire Analysis
code: library(tcrdistR) data(dash)  # Build a TCRrep object (deduplicates identical clones per subject) rep <- TCRrep(dash, organism = "mouse", compute_distances = TRUE) rep #> TCRrep with 1888 clones (mouse, AB chains) #>   paired_dist: 1888 x 1888  # Pairwise distance heatmap plot_tcrdist_heatmap(rep@paired_dist[1:40, 1:40])  # Per-component distances (CDR3-only, V-region-only, etc.) d_cdr3 <- tcrdist_matrix(rep@clone_df, "mouse", components = "cdr3") d_v    <- tcrdist_matrix(rep@clone_df, "mouse", components = "v_region")  # Single-chain mode (beta-only input, no alpha columns needed) beta_only <- rep@clone_df[, c("vb", "cdr3b")] d_beta <- tcrdist_matrix(beta_only, "mouse")  # Kernel PCA pca <- compute_tcrdist_kernel_pca(   rep@clone_df, rep@organism, n_components = 50L ) plot_tcr_scatter(   pca$embeddings[, 1:2],   color_by = rep@clone_df$epitope,   title = "Kernel PCA",   point_size = 1.5 )  # UMAP (uses TCRdist KNN neighbors directly) umap <- compute_tcrdist_umap(rep@clone_df, rep@organism, seed = 42) plot_tcr_scatter(   umap$embeddings,   color_by = rep@clone_df$epitope,   axis_label_prefix = "UMAP",   point_size = 1.5 )

title: Generalized Simpson's diversity (Hill numbers framework) — tcr_diversity
text: diversity index \(Z_r\) probability \(r\) randomly drawn individuals (without replacement) belong species: $$Z_r = \sum_i \frac{c_i}{n} \prod_{k=1}^{r-1} \frac{c_i - k}{n - k}$$ \(c_i\) count clonotype \(\) \(n = \sum c_i\). returned entropy \(1 - Z_r\) (probability drawing \(r\) different species). \(r=2\) classical Simpson's diversity. effective number species (Hill number) : \(D = 1 / Z_r^{1/(r-1)}\). Confidence intervals use delta method multinomial variance \(Z_r\). \(r=2\), exact gradient \(\partial Z / \partial p_i = 2 p_i\) used; higher orders, approximation \(r \cdot p_i^{r-1}\) applied.

Per-component decomposition via components parameter (CDR3, V-region, single-chain, custom combinations). Single-chain auto-detection beta-alpha-data. core computation C++ via Rcpp.

title: tcrdistR 0.1.0
text: K-nearest neighbors (tcrdist_knn()), radius neighbors (tcrdist_radius_neighbors()). KNN precomputed matrices (knn_from_matrix()) PCA embeddings (knn_from_pca()).

title: tcrdistR 0.1.0
text: Kernel PCA linear Gaussian kernels (compute_tcrdist_kernel_pca()). UMAP via KNN PCA path (compute_tcrdist_umap()).

title: tcrdistR 0.1.0
text: Neighborhood enrichment testing (neighborhood_test()). TCR clumping detection background resampling (find_clumping()). Meta-clonotype discovery across subjects (find_meta_clonotypes()). Database matching significance testing (match_tcrs_to_db()).
